os-net-http.title: HTTP client
os-net-http.summary: Named HTTP clients from plain settings, with headers, retries, timeouts, a concurrency limit and a safe mode for links you don't trust.

gives.1: Describe an API once, in code or in a config file, and get a ready client with its base address, headers and timeout.
gives.2: Get results, not exceptions: every call returns an `OSResult` with a status and a stable code.
gives.3: Fetch links from users without letting them reach your own network, and without reading an unlimited body.

sample.call: Call a JSON API and get a result
sample.safe-fetch: Fetch a link from a user safely

clients.title: Clients and settings
clients.summary: Describe an API with `ApiConfig` and register it with `AddOSHttp`.

1.title: Describe an API
1.text: `ApiConfig` holds the name, base address, timeout and headers.

2.title: Register a client
2.text: `AddOSHttp` validates the settings and registers a named client.

3.title: Works from JSON
3.text: The same settings work in a config file or JSON with kebab-case names.

4.title: Ready-made headers
4.text: Each header has a `Type`, such as `BearerAuth` or `ApiKey`.

1.title: ApiConfig fields
1.text:
An `ApiConfig` has a `Name`, an optional `BaseUrl`, a `Timeout` and the number of `Retries`.

`PermitLimit` and `QueueLimit` are optional. `MaxBytes` is the body size cap, `Safe` is the safe-mode switch and `Headers` is the list of headers.

2.title: Registering and names
2.text:
`AddOSHttp` validates the config and registers a named client on `IHttpClientFactory`. It also adds the headers and the resilience pipeline. Registering a name twice throws.

The same names work in a config file or JSON: `name`, `base-url`, `timeout`, `retries`, `permit-limit`, `queue-limit`, `max-bytes`, `safe`, `headers` and `extras`. The `timeout` value is a time span such as `00:00:20`.

3.title: Header types
3.text:
Each header has a `Type`. `Own` uses its `Name` and `Value`.

`Accept`, `UserAgent`, `ApiVersion` and `ApiKey` set well-known headers. `BearerAuth` sends `Value` as a token and `BasicAuth` builds the value from `User` and `Password`.

`ContentType` applies to requests that have a body. A header the request already has is not replaced.

config.title: Read a client from JSON
config.note: Header types are written by name, and a timeout is a time span, not a number.

headers.title: Send credentials and fixed headers
headers.note: Credentials are added to every request, so they never go into the URL.

type.ApiConfig: The settings of one API client.
type.ApiHeader: One header, either fixed text or credentials.
type.ApiHeaderType: What a header means, and how its value is sent.
type.HttpClientEx: Registration of clients on the service collection.

ApiConfig.Name: The name you pass to `IOSHttp.Create`. Required and unique.
ApiConfig.BaseUrl: The address that relative endpoints are added to.
ApiConfig.Timeout: The time one attempt may take. When it is not set, the standard 10 seconds per attempt apply.
ApiConfig.Retries: How many times a safe request is repeated after a transient failure. 3 by default; 0 turns retries off.
ApiConfig.PermitLimit: The most requests sent at the same time.
ApiConfig.QueueLimit: How many more requests may wait when the limit is reached.
ApiConfig.MaxBytes: The largest response body that is read, 10 MiB by default.
ApiConfig.Safe: Turns on the safe mode for untrusted links.
ApiConfig.Headers: The headers added to every request.
ApiConfig.Extras: Free text values for your own code. The library does not read them.

ApiHeader.Type: What kind of header this is.
ApiHeader.Name: The header name, for `Own`, and optionally for `ApiKey`.

HttpClientEx.AddOSHttp: Registers one client or a list of clients. It throws for a missing or repeated name.
HttpClientEx.GetConfig: Finds a config in a list by name, ignoring case. Throws when it is missing.

calls.title: Making calls
calls.summary: Get a client by name and call it; every answer is an `OSResult`.

1.title: Get a client
1.text: `IOSHttp.Create(name)` gives an `IApiService` for a registered client.

2.title: Every answer a result
2.text: A 2xx answer is `Ok`; any other status becomes a failed result with the code `http.<status>`.

3.title: Known failures
3.text: Network problems, timeouts and big bodies each have their own code.

4.title: Safe repeats
4.text: A request that is not safe is never sent again.

1.title: The methods
1.text:
`IOSHttp.Create(name)` gives an `IApiService` for a registered client.

`GetAsync<T>`, `PostAsync`, `PutAsync` and `DeleteAsync` send JSON and read JSON. `GetStringAsync` returns the body text.

`FetchAsync` returns an `ApiFetch` with the status, the final address after redirects, the media type and the body. It does not judge the status.

2.title: Answers and codes
2.text:
A 2xx answer is `Ok`. Any other status becomes a failed result whose code is `http.<status>`. Its status follows `ResultEx.FromHttpStatus`, so 404 is `NotFound` and 429 is `Unavailable`.

Network problems give `Unavailable` with `http.network` and a timeout gives `http.timeout`. A body over the limit gives `http.too-large` and a bad endpoint gives `http.endpoint`.

3.title: Cancelling and repeats
3.text:
Cancelling the token still throws, as .NET does.

A request is never retried unless it is safe, so a POST is sent once.

get.title: Read a JSON answer
get.note: Check Succeeded before using Data. A 404 is a NotFound result, not an exception.

post.title: Send a JSON body
post.note: The body is serialized as UTF-8 JSON. A POST is never repeated automatically.

fetch.title: Read a page without judging its status
fetch.note: Succeeded means the server answered; IsOk tells whether the status was 2xx.

status.title: See how a status becomes a result
status.note: The result code is http. followed by the number.

type.IOSHttp: Creates the service for a registered client by name.
type.ApiService: The default IApiService, built on one HttpClient and its settings.
type.ApiFetch: A page as it came back: status, addresses, media type and body.
type.HttpCodes: The error codes of this package.
type.ApiRequest: An endpoint, a method (GET by default) and an optional JSON body, for sending one request as a value.

IOSHttp.Create: Returns the service for a client name. Throws if the name is not registered.

IApiService.GetAsync: Sends GET and reads the body as JSON.
IApiService.GetStringAsync: Sends GET and returns the body as text.
IApiService.FetchAsync: Sends GET and returns the whole answer, whatever its status.
IApiService.PostAsync: Sends a JSON body with POST.
IApiService.PutAsync: Sends a JSON body with PUT.
IApiService.SendAsync: Sends an ApiRequest with any method and returns the whole answer, like FetchAsync.

ApiFetch.Url: The address that was asked for.
ApiFetch.MediaType: The media type of the body, such as text/html.
ApiFetch.IsRedirected: True when the final address differs from the asked one.

HttpCodes.Endpoint: The endpoint is empty, not a valid address, or not allowed in safe mode.
HttpCodes.Blocked: The address points to a private or local network.
HttpCodes.Timeout: The call took longer than its time limit.
HttpCodes.Network: The server could not be reached.
HttpCodes.TooLarge: The body is larger than MaxBytes.
HttpCodes.Format: The body is not the JSON that was expected.
HttpCodes.Status: Builds the code of a status, such as http.404.

safety.title: Safe mode
safety.summary: Fetch links you don't trust without opening a way into your own network.

1.title: Why safe mode
1.text: Your server fetches a user's link and could end up reading its own network.

2.title: Public only
2.text: With `Safe = true` it connects only to public addresses.

3.title: Hard limits
3.text: At most five redirects and a body cap of `MaxBytes`.

1.title: The risk
1.text:
When a user can submit a link, your server fetches it for them.

A link to `http://169.254.169.254/` or `http://10.0.0.5/` would make the server read its own network.

2.title: What safe mode does
2.text:
Set `Safe = true`. The client accepts only plain `http` and `https` links without a login. It resolves the host itself and connects only to public addresses.

So a name that points to a private address is refused at connection time, even after a redirect.

3.title: Limits and errors
3.text:
It follows at most five redirects, limits the response headers and stops reading a body at `MaxBytes`.

A refused address gives `Forbidden` with `http.blocked`, and an oversized body gives `Failed` with `http.too-large`. `AddressRules.IsPublic` is the rule used, and you can call it yourself.

addresses.title: Tell public addresses from private ones
addresses.note: Loopback, private ranges, link-local addresses such as the cloud metadata address, and unique-local IPv6 are all refused.

enable.title: Fetch a user's link in safe mode
enable.note: Branch on the code, not on text. The page is read only up to MaxBytes.

type.AddressRules: The rule for which network addresses a safe client may connect to.

AddressRules.IsPublic: False for loopback, private, link-local, carrier-grade, multicast and unspecified addresses.

resilience.title: Retries and limits
resilience.summary: Every client gets Microsoft's standard resilience pipeline, set from the config.

2.title: Timeout
2.text: `Timeout` sets the time for one attempt.

1.title: The pipeline
1.text:
Each client uses `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience`, which replaced the older Polly-based package.

The pipeline limits concurrent requests and applies a total timeout. It retries transient failures with an exponential delay. It breaks the circuit when a server keeps failing, and it times out each attempt.

2.title: Timeout and concurrency
2.text:
`Timeout` sets the time for one attempt. The total time becomes the attempts times `Timeout` plus 30 seconds.

`PermitLimit` and `QueueLimit` bound the concurrent requests.

3.title: Retries
3.text:
`Retries` sets the number of retries and applies only to safe methods. POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE are sent once, because repeating them could create a second order or send a second SMS.

Set `Retries = 0` to turn retries off for every method. A failed attempt returns `Unavailable` with the code `http.timeout` or `http.network`.

configure.title: Set the timeout, retries and concurrency
configure.note: At most 20 requests run together and 50 may wait; a failed GET is retried twice.

no-retries.title: Turn retries off
no-retries.note: Use it for a service that is not idempotent in any way.
